blocks.text: Most of your Zoom work on a Mac is not hosting. It is scheduling, moving, and fixing meetings that belong to someone else. Zoom built a feature for this job called scheduling privilege. It lets one user create and manage meetings on behalf of another. Zoom's support article covers the steps for the desktop app on Windows, macOS, and Linux together, so labels can differ a little by version.
What Zoom for executive assistants on Mac covers

Zoom has no separate assistant app. You use the same Zoom Workplace app your executive uses. The difference is the permission. Without scheduling privilege, you cannot pick your executive in the Schedule for drop-down. With it, you can create, edit, and cancel their meetings. Zoom also says you can change who hosts an existing meeting from the Schedule For section.

Most assistants handle three jobs in Zoom. They book new calls, they move calls when a client changes plans, and they fix the host when someone else needs to run the room. All three use the same Schedule screen. The mistakes happen when you assume the permission is in place before you check it.
Why scheduling takes so much of an assistant's week

Calendar work is the hidden load behind every executive's day. The Harvard number explains why. A leader in back-to-back meetings needs someone to hold the calendar steady. Calendly's survey shows the same pressure among ordinary workers, with scheduling time rising from the year before.

No study I found measures how much time executive assistants spend on Zoom scheduling in particular. Treat these numbers as context, not as your own benchmark. Track your own week for two weeks. Write down how long each invite, move, and host change takes. That list tells you what to fix first.
Set up scheduling privilege before your first invite

Setup belongs to your executive, not to you. Cornell IT describes the flow used at their university, and Zoom's article matches it. The executive signs in to the Zoom web settings and opens Settings > Meetings > Other > Schedule Privilege. Then they add your email and save. Work through the steps in this order.

items: Ask your executive to sign in to Zoom in a browser.
Go to Settings > Meetings > Other > Schedule Privilege.
Click Add, enter your email address, and click Save.
Tick the optional boxes only if you need them. Cornell lists private events, cloud recordings, and reports.
Sign out of the Zoom Workplace app on your Mac, then sign back in.
Open the app and check that Schedule for appears on the Schedule screen.

blocks.text: Zoom says an admin must enable scheduling privilege as well. If the option never appears, ask your IT team to check the admin setting before you retry the steps. Your executive's license matters too. Zoom's article says both users must be Licensed or On-Prem, on the same account or linked master and sub accounts.

Worked example: your executive is in Chicago and the client is in Denver. You set the new call in your executive's time zone, then read the time again in the client's zone before you click Save. A time error in an invite is cheap to fix before it goes out. It is expensive after the client has planned a day around it.
Schedule a meeting for your executive in the Zoom app

Open the Zoom Workplace app and click Schedule on the Home tab. Open the Schedule for drop-down and choose your executive. Set the topic, the time, and the settings you need. Click Save. Zoom's article lists the same path for the desktop app on every platform it covers.

Menu names move between versions. If a label is missing, look for the Schedule for drop-down first. It is the control that makes the whole flow work. If it is missing, the most likely cause is the privilege, not the Mac.

If you cannot find Schedule, check which account you are signed in to. Scheduling privilege only works between users on the same account or linked accounts. Sign out, sign in with the right account, and try again.
Change the host of a meeting you already scheduled

Hosts matter more than most assistants expect. The host runs the room. If your executive needs to lead a call that someone else created, change the host instead of rebuilding the meeting. Rebuilding means new links, new invites, and a second round of confusion for the attendees.

To change the host, open the meeting in the Zoom Workplace app and go to the Schedule For section. Choose the new host from the drop-down and save. Both users still need the privilege and a licensed account for this to work.

Webinars follow stricter rules. Zoom says both users need the webinar add-on before you can schedule one for another user. Confirm that before you promise a webinar to a client. A regular meeting will not do the job if the client expects registration.
Use Zoom meeting templates for calls you repeat

Templates save time on calls you repeat, like weekly one-on-ones or board prep sessions. Zoom documents templates in the web portal. Sign in, click Meetings, then pick a template from the Template drop-down in Schedule a Meeting. You can also open the Meeting Templates tab.

A meeting created from a template fills in the current date and time. Change the date before you save, or the call lands on the wrong day. Check the host field too. Zoom's template article does not say whether alternative hosts carry over, so look before you send.

Admin templates need a Business, Education, or Enterprise account. Zoom's article does not state a limit on how many templates you can keep. Some guides say the Mac app can save a meeting as a template, and they mention a cap. Zoom's own article does not say that, so test the Mac app on your version before you rely on it.
Fix the errors that stop scheduling on Mac

Most scheduling failures come from three causes. The privilege is missing, the license is wrong, or you are on a different account. Check those three before you touch anything else. Each one has a clear fix, and none needs a reinstall.

items: Schedule for is missing: the privilege is not set, or you have not signed out and back in.
Error 3003 when you edit or cancel for another user: check privileges and license status, as Zoom advises.
Your executive is not in the drop-down: confirm both users are licensed and on the same account or linked accounts.
Webinar options are missing: the webinar add-on is needed for both users.

blocks.text: Lazur helps with this kind of error. Hold ⌥⌘ (Option and Command) and ask what the message says. Lazur answers out loud. It can circle the Settings control so you know where to look. It will not change the setting for you, so the fix stays in your hands and your executive's.
Keep the Zoom app updated on your Mac

Out-of-date builds cause odd bugs, and the scheduling screen is not immune. Zoom says Mac users can check for updates by clicking their profile picture and choosing Check for Updates. When an update is available, Zoom shows a pop-up within 24 hours of login.

Zoom labels updates as mandatory or optional. Read the pop-up before you click. Do not wait for a mandatory update on the morning of a client call. Update the day before, reopen the app, and test Schedule for on a throwaway meeting.
Dictate agendas and invites with fn

Assistants type the same agenda text many times. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictate the agenda into the meeting description, then read it back once before you save. Reading it back catches the names that the dictation tool misses.

Lazur also keeps snippets, a personal dictionary, and clipboard slots. Use the dictionary for names that get misspelled, like client surnames or product names. Save a snippet for the dial-in line or the reminder you send before every board call.
Mistakes executive assistants make with Zoom scheduling

items: Scheduling before checking privilege. Look at the Schedule for drop-down first, every time you start.
Forgetting to sign out and back in after the privilege is granted. The option stays hidden until you do.
Changing a time without checking the zone. Read it in your executive's zone and the client's before you save.
Assuming a template sets the host. Check the host field after you load a template.
Ignoring the update pop-up. Read it before the next client call, not after.

blocks.text: How Lazur fits into a scheduling day

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur also handles everyday work by voice. Set a timer, add an Apple Reminders item to check the attendee list, or add a Calendar event for the prep call. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs and comes back with a summary and a report.

Privacy matters when you share a screen with client details. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Zoom or any other app. Think of it as a sharp colleague who can see your screen and point at the right control.

Your first week with Zoom scheduling

items: Ask your executive to grant you scheduling privilege today.
Sign out of the Zoom Workplace app and sign back in.
Confirm that Schedule for appears on the Home tab's Schedule screen.
Book one test meeting for yourself, set a different host, and save.
Delete the test meeting and note any step that took longer than expected.

blocks.text: Once the test works, start with your executive's next routine call. Keep a short list of every host change and template you use. That list becomes your checklist for the next busy week. faq.question: Can an executive assistant schedule Zoom meetings on a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, once your executive grants scheduling privilege. Zoom's article says you sign in to the desktop app, click Schedule on the Home tab, open the Schedule for drop-down, choose the user, and click Save. Both of you need a licensed account on the same account or linked accounts, and an admin must enable the feature.

faq.question: Why don't I see the Schedule for drop-down on my Mac?
faq.answer: The usual cause is a missing privilege or a stale session. Ask your executive to add you under Settings > Meetings > Other > Schedule Privilege. Then sign out of the Zoom Workplace app and sign back in. If it still does not show, ask your IT team to confirm your license and the admin setting.

faq.question: What does error 3003 mean for scheduling?
faq.answer: Zoom's guidance says a 3003 error when you edit or cancel a meeting for another user means you should check privileges and license status. Confirm that both accounts are licensed and on the same account, then try again.

faq.question: Can I change the host of a meeting after I scheduled it?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the meeting, go to the Schedule For section, choose the new host from the drop-down, and save. Both users still need the scheduling privilege and licensed accounts for this to work.

faq.question: Do Zoom meeting templates work in the Mac app?
faq.answer: Zoom documents templates in the web portal, through Meetings and the Template drop-down in Schedule a Meeting. Some guides describe the Mac app differently, and Zoom's article does not confirm it. Test the Mac app on your version. Admin templates need a Business, Education, or Enterprise account.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons or schedule the meeting for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at controls, draws a circle around them, and guides you one click at a time. You do the clicks. Lazur also answers questions out loud and drafts text, which it can type where your cursor is when you ask.

faq.question: What happens to my screen when I use Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut, ⌥⌘. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer the question. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.
